papers.title: Nyx: a flexible framework for sleep scoring across species, lifespan and modalities.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Nyx is an unsupervised sleep-scoring framework based on principal component analysis that flexibly clusters epochs into sleep states. Validated on ~8,000 hours across 19 datasets, it generalizes across species, lifespan, modalities, and altered sleep architectures, matching human inter-scorer agreement and enabling real-time closed-loop manipulation.

papers.title: Sleep dynamics and epileptogenesis following Kainic acid in epilepsy-susceptible (DBA/2 J) and epilepsy-resistant (C57BL/6) mice.
papers.summary: This study compared sleep dynamics and epileptogenesis in epilepsy-susceptible DBA/2J and epilepsy-resistant C57BL/6 mice after kainic acid treatment, finding that DBA mice had more severe seizures, lower baseline slow wave activity, and impaired sleep homeostasis, suggesting that baseline sleep abnormalities may increase vulnerability to epileptogenesis.

papers.title: Backpropagation-Free Test-Time Adaptation for Lightweight EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interfaces.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: This paper proposes Backpropagation-Free Transformations (BFT), a test-time adaptation method for EEG-based brain-computer interfaces that avoids backpropagation by using sample-wise transformations and a learning-to-rank module. Experiments on five EEG datasets demonstrate its effectiveness, versatility, robustness, and efficiency, enabling lightweight plug-and-play BCIs.

papers.title: Diphenhydramine Disrupts Sleep Architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's Disease Model and Wild-Type Mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study tested chronic diphenhydramine (DPH) treatment on sleep architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's disease model mice and wild-type littermates using EEG/EMG telemetry. DPH fragmented NREM2 sleep in both genotypes, increased NREM1 and REM during the active phase, and exacerbated NREM2 fragmentation in 5XFAD mice, questioning its use as a sleep aid in AD.

papers.title: Neural Signatures of Conscious Experience During Sleep: A Serial Awakening Study Using High-Density EEG
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG and serial awakenings in 140 participants, the study identified neural signatures of dreaming during NREM sleep. Dreaming was associated with reduced alpha/delta power and increased gamma measures posteriorly, and machine learning classifiers reached an ROC-AUC of 0.80, revealing reproducible posterior electrophysiological markers of consciousness.

papers.title: SCORE: Subject Coordinate Recovery for Label-Free Cross-Subject EEG-to-Image Retrieval
papers.summary: This paper presents SCORE, a label-free framework for cross-subject EEG-to-image retrieval that aligns EEG coordinates across subjects without target labels, achieving significant improvements over baselines on two benchmarks.

papers.title: Robust time delay estimation for measurement of ictal EEG traveling waves.
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluated methodological factors affecting time delay estimation of ictal traveling waves in intracranial EEG, finding that accurate estimation requires wave speeds <1000 mm/s, coherence >0.4, corner referencing, high sampling rates, and electrode spacing ≤3 mm, and it identified novel propagation patterns in human data.

papers.title: General-purpose time-series foundation models enable sample-efficient transfer learning in retinal electrophysiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates the use of general-purpose time-series foundation models for electroretinography (ERG) analysis via transfer learning, finding that frozen and fine-tuned embeddings, especially with multimodal metadata, perform best on classification tasks. Performance was maintained with as few as 300 records, supporting the practicality of this approach.

papers.title: Generalizability of EEG-Based Dementia Classifiers: A Multicenter study of Alzheimer's, MCI, And FTD.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This multicenter study evaluated EEG-based machine-learning classifiers for dementia subtypes (CN, MCI, AD, FTD), addressing imbalance and cross-center generalizability. CN vs AD showed robust cross-center performance, while CN vs MCI and FTD contrasts were heterogeneous and limited, emphasizing the need for strict validation and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Cognitive exertion reshapes resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan
papers.summary: This study examines how cognitive exertion affects resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan, finding that post-task recordings show widespread slowing of individual alpha peak frequency and age-dependent changes in the aperiodic exponent. These results demonstrate that these markers are state-dependent and post-task recordings may be useful for indexing individual differences.

papers.title: Moving beyond spike detection: High frequency-driven masking improves seizure onset zone localization in intracranial electroencephalography.
papers.summary: The study benchmarked eight interictal spike detection algorithms in intracranial EEG from 35 epilepsy patients, finding that spike detection alone has limited seizure onset zone (SOZ) localization (ratios .23-.51). Masking spikes to include only those co-occurring with high-frequency oscillations markedly improved localization (median ratio .89), outperforming spikes or HFOs alone.

papers.title: Interpretable machine-learning for depression classification based on a three-component EEG marker.
papers.summary: This pilot study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework for depression classification using a three-component EEG marker (coherence heterogeneity and asymmetry variability). RBF-SVM achieved AUC 0.910 under subject-wise validation, with SHAP identifying gamma-band coherence and beta asymmetry as key contributors.

papers.title: Graph-Based Approaches to Learning Epileptogenic Zone Localization Using Stereo-EEG Recordings
papers.summary: This paper compares graph-based models for localizing the epileptogenic zone from resting-state stereo-EEG in 40 patients, showing that a proposed Region-Bridge-c topology achieves the best performance at reduced edge density, and that optimal graph topology varies by patient.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
papers.summary: Using simultaneous multi-region Neuropixels recordings in 35 mice, this preprint found that psilocybin selectively reconfigures burst firing, not mean firing rates, across cortex, thalamus, and hippocampus. These burst effects were largely abolished by ketanserin, indicating 5-HT2A receptor dependence.

papers.title: MDAGCN: A multimodal dynamic adaptive graph convolutional network for sleep staging.
papers.summary: The paper introduces MDAGCN, a multimodal dynamic adaptive graph convolutional network for sleep staging that uses specialized branches for EEG, EOG, EMG, and ECG. On ISRUC-S3 and Sleep-EDF-78, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and kappa, improving over baselines by up to 0.6 percentage points.

papers.title: Brain network biomarkers for diagnosis and clinical stratification in multiple sclerosis: a longitudinal study integrating individualised structural covariance MRI with high-density EEG.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of 635 MS patients and controls identified reproducible structural covariance network abnormalities in MS, particularly involving thalamic and visual networks, with connectivity features best for diagnosis and topological features for clinical stratification.

papers.title: Aperiodic EEG activity is a domain-specific marker of attentional aging in neurotypical adults.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This longitudinal study tracked aperiodic EEG activity and behavior over ~5 years in neurotypical adults. They found that within-person decline in aperiodic activity was specifically associated with changes in sustained attention reaction times, but not executive function, suggesting it as a domain-specific biomarker of attentional aging.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG microstate dynamics reflect individual differences in tactile angle discriminability.
papers.summary: This study examined resting-state EEG microstates in 81 participants and found that microstate A occurrence was the strongest predictor of tactile angle discrimination threshold (β = -0.40). Higher microstate A occurrence correlated with better tactile acuity, suggesting a candidate neurophysiological index for tactile spatial acuity.

papers.title: EEG CONNECT: A proposed reporting checklist for EEG-based connectivity studies in clinical epilepsy research.
papers.summary: The authors propose EEG CONNECT, a 24-item reporting checklist for EEG-based connectivity studies in epilepsy research, and test it on 45 recent clinical studies. Mean reporting adherence was 70.3%, with underreporting of connectivity estimation, biological plausibility, and limitations; adherence correlated with journal impact factor and citation rate.

papers.title: Distributed EEG power asymmetries across frequencies in PTSD: Introducing the dynamic EEG power differential (DEPD) index.
papers.summary: This study introduces the Dynamic EEG Power Differential (DEPD) index to quantify distributed, frequency-specific hemispheric power asymmetries. Using resting-state EEG in PTSD and controls, they found that distributed inter- and intra-hemispheric power differentials, especially non-frontal and non-alpha, better distinguished PTSD and correlated with symptom severity than conventional frontal alpha asymmetry.

papers.title: Large-Scale In Vivo Electrophysiology Analysis Reveals Opposing Thalamic and Hippocampal Excitability After Third-Trimester-Equivalent Alcohol Exposure in Mice.
papers.summary: This study performed high-density in vivo electrophysiological recordings in behaving mice after third-trimester-equivalent alcohol exposure, sampling 7,490 neurons. They found reduced firing rates overall, with hippocampal hyperexcitability and thalamic dysfunction, achieving 80% accuracy in classifying neurons by treatment based on electrophysiological properties.

papers.title: DRDNet: A dual-view representation decoupling network for handwriting imagery EEG classification.
papers.summary: This paper proposes DRDNet, a dual-view representation decoupling network for classifying handwriting imagery EEG in brain-computer interfaces. The network achieves 67.74% and 62.51% average accuracy on two tasks, outperforming seven baselines, demonstrating effective decoupling of continuous temporal trends and local high-response patterns.

papers.title: Hybrid novice-AI system achieves expert-level performance in intraoperative ischemia detection.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study developed a hybrid novice-AI system for detecting intraoperative cerebral ischemia from continuous EEG. Compared to novices alone and AI alone, the hybrid was non-inferior to experts in sensitivity and false-positive rate, and improved precision-recall and calibration, suggesting potential for expert-level monitoring with limited expert availability.

papers.title: Machine learning to detect intraoperative ischemia from electroencephalography in carotid endarterectomy surgery.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study evaluated machine learning models for detecting cerebral ischemia during carotid endarterectomy using quantitative EEG features. Random forest achieved highest sensitivity and area under precision-recall curve, while XGBoost showed highest specificity; alpha-band activity and hemispheric asymmetry were most discriminative.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic Transient Beta Event Rates in Autism and Related Neurogenetic Conditions.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study compared transient beta event (TBE) rates in EEG across children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), related neurogenetic conditions, and typically developing controls. Elevated TBE rates were found in some ASD and a majority of Phelan-McDermid, Rett, and SYNGAP1 conditions, suggesting TBE rate as a stratification biomarker with divergent and convergent properties.

papers.title: Engineering a Timing-Accurate VR-EEG-Oculomotor Fusion System for Objective Assessment of Executive Function in ADHD.
papers.summary: The authors developed a timing-accurate VR-EEG-oculomotor system for the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test and validated stimulus-onset timing. In 101 children (64 ADHD, 37 control), a deep neural network fusing task performance, head rotation, eye movement, and N2/P3 ERPs achieved 83% accuracy in classifying ADHD, demonstrating multimodal integration for objective assessment.

papers.title: Cortical dynamics of adolescent and adult semi-skilled soccer players during execution of the passing skill: An EEG study.
papers.summary: This study compared EEG oscillatory activity during soccer passing in adolescent and adult semi-skilled players. Adolescents showed higher theta and alpha relative power than adults, while beta power showed a group by region interaction, indicating age-related differences in cortical engagement during passing.

papers.title: Visuomotor mismatch EEG responses over occipital cortex of freely moving human subjects.
papers.summary: This study combined wireless EEG with a VR headset to test for visuomotor mismatch responses in freely moving humans. They found robust mismatch responses in occipital cortex with reversed polarity and higher power than visual and oddball mismatch responses, analogous to those in mice.

papers.title: Validation of intraoperative processed electroencephalography and cerebral oximetry for prediction of postoperative delirium in cardiac surgery: a prospective observational study.
papers.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
papers.summary: This prospective observational study validates combined intraoperative monitoring using processed EEG and cerebral oximetry to predict postoperative delirium in cardiac surgery. It finds that longer time in certain combined states increases delirium odds and that longer time in State 1 increases persistent organ dysfunction.

papers.title: Evaluating the performance of EEG based on ANN to predict the effectiveness of tDCS combined evaluative conditioning on obsession symptoms reduction in contamination OCD patients: Secondary analysis of data from a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial used EEG features and artificial neural networks to predict the effectiveness of tDCS combined with evaluative conditioning in contamination OCD patients. The optimized feedforward network achieved an RMSE of 0.57, indicating feasibility of predicting individual Y-BOCS score changes from pre-intervention EEG.

papers.title: EEG-ECeG Coherence Mapping of Human Cerebro-cerebellar Projections: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: The authors recorded EEG and electro-cerebellogram (ECeG) during finger movements in six healthy adults and used wavelet coherence to map cerebro-cerebellar connectivity. They observed movement-related delta/theta coherence patterns consistent with crossed cerebro-cerebellar projections, supporting the utility of ECeG for non-invasive imaging.

papers.title: Dynamic Hemispheric Lateralization of Naturalistic Emotional Processing After Unilateral Stroke: An EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 15 left-hemisphere stroke, 15 right-hemisphere stroke, and 15 healthy controls, the authors examined dynamic hemispheric lateralization during naturalistic emotional processing using EEG. They found that parietal-theta lateralization index dynamics differed by hemisphere group, with right-hemisphere patients showing increased switching and entropy during positive clips, suggesting a stability-flexibility imbalance.

papers.title: EEG Connectomics in Rotator Cuff Injury: Central Network Reorganization During Three-Plane Antagonistic Shoulder Tasks.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: This study characterized central nervous system reorganization in rotator cuff injury during three-plane antagonistic shoulder tasks using EEG connectomics. They found frequency-specific over-integration/under-segregation in beta and low-gamma bands and robust classification (ACC≈0.86) using graph metrics.

papers.title: Ketogenic diet attenuates seizures by promoting lipid droplet formation via peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma signaling pathway.
papers.summary: This study investigates the antiseizure mechanism of the ketogenic diet in a mouse model of temporal lobe epilepsy. It finds that the diet upregulates perilipin 1 via the PPARγ pathway, promoting lipid droplet formation and reducing neuronal excitability, providing a novel mechanistic link.

papers.title: Separating early and intermediate vision EEG signatures of facial emotion recognition in a fast divided attention task to eye and mouth features.
papers.summary: This study investigated EEG signatures of facial emotion recognition under fast divided attention to eye and mouth features. They found that the N170 and P250 components were modulated by emotional expression, while the P100 was not.

papers.title: Responsibility cannot be abdicated: rigour, proportionate evidence, and full electroencephalography-informed care in perioperative brain health. Response to Br J Anaesth 2026; 137: 269-70.
papers.summary: This letter responds to a prior article, arguing for rigorous, proportionate evidence and full EEG-informed care in perioperative brain health, emphasizing that responsibility cannot be abdicated despite monitoring challenges.

papers.title: Wavelet-based assessment of postural stability in young female volleyball players using a baroresistive platform.
papers.summary: This study used wavelet analysis to evaluate postural stability in young female volleyball players using a baroresistive platform. They found discriminative properties in frequency ranges associated with visual and vestibular control.

papers.title: Dielectrophoresis and ζ-potential as potential low-cost complements to patch clamp for measurement of cell electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This study demonstrated that dielectrophoresis (DEP) and electrophoretic light scattering (ELS) can provide cost-effective alternatives to patch clamp for measuring cell electrophysiology. Results showed DEP yields resting membrane potential and membrane conductance values highly comparable to patch clamp data.

papers.title: Individual and Community-Level Differences in Use of Contemporary Electrophysiology Procedures in the United States.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: This national study analyzed Medicare claims from 2018-2021 to examine trends and sociodemographic differences in the use of four contemporary electrophysiology procedures. It found that rates of pulmonary vein isolation, left atrial appendage occlusion, and leadless pacemaker implantation increased, while subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator use declined, with significant disparities by race, social vulnerability, and region.

papers.title: ICE Catheter as Transesophageal Probe in Children With Congenital Heart Disease Undergoing an Electrophysiology Study.
papers.summary: This case series describes the use of an intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) catheter as a transesophageal probe in six infants and young children with congenital heart disease undergoing electrophysiology studies. The technique provided high-quality anatomical guidance and avoided large-bore venous access.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
